title: unified tool-caller API + delayed-commit retry semantics to stabilize streaming and multi-tool results
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a unified Tool Caller API that offers deterministic semantics for multi-tool and parallel tool invocations, streaming stability fixes, and a delayed-commit idempotent retry strategy to reduce duplicate side effects.
commits: Initial unified-tool-caller skeleton and interface definitions
Implement delayed-commit retry coordinator and idempotency token plumbing
Integrate deterministic multi-call ordering and deterministic response merge
Stabilize streaming hooks and add per-tool streaming checkpoints
Add Python and TypeScript SDK shims and compatibility layer tests
Docs and migration guide for existing consumers
Fix: e2e flaky scenario in tool composition test
description: Context and motivation: Customers frequently surface two pain points when composing LLM responses with external tools: 1) streaming instability when tool results and model tokens interleave mid-stream, and 2) duplicate side-effects from naive retry semantics for parallel tool calls. This PR introduces a unified 'Tool Caller' API and a delayed-commit retry strategy to address both issues in a developer-friendly, OpenAI-compatible surface. Design summary: The Tool Caller provides a single entrypoint for: a) orchestrating ordered or parallel tool invocations with deterministic merge semantics, b) registering streaming checkpoints so the model can safely stream partial token output without observing incomplete tool side-effects, and c) delayed-commit retries that only expose tool results to the model after idempotency checks pass. Streaming stability is handled via per-tool stream checkpoints plus a small bounded rebuffer window to preserve low-latency streaming while avoiding mid-stream observable state changes. The retry model uses idempotency tokens and a delayed commit phase: tool runs return provisional results that are not yet injected into the model stream; on success and idempotency confirmation we atomically commit the result into the model's context. Implementation highlights: server/api/tool_caller.py defines the ToolCaller class and public HTTP/SDK surface. server/streaming/stream_manager.py implements streaming checkpoints, rebuffer window, and backpressure integration. server/runtime/tool_dispatcher.cpp contains the low-level executor changes for parallel task orchestration and idempotency hooks. SDK shims (sdk/python/redwood/tools.py and sdk/typescript/src/tool-client.ts) expose the new call signature while preserving the old openai-compatible helpers via a compatibility layer. Observability: introduced tool_caller_latency and tool_commit_success metrics and added a small dashboard tile. Tests: new integration test (tests/integration/tool_composition_test.py) covers ordered, parallel, failure+retry, and streaming-snapshot scenarios. CI: added a targeted e2e workflow ci/workflows/tool-e2e.yml. Migration notes: The compatibility layer keeps old helper names; consumers that depended on streaming-mid-tool injections should migrate to the new two-phase commit injection model. See docs/migration/tool-caller-migration.md for a step-by-step guide and sample code. Rollout plan: feature-gate the new API for hosted and dedicated deployments for four weeks, shadow traffic for two days, then enable for 10% of main traffic for a week before full ramp. Monitoring will focus on commit latency, duplicate-effect rate, and streaming rebuffer tail latency. Backout plan: revert feature flag and disable delayed commits; hotfix branch created if we see increased error budgets. Benchmarks: internal perf runs show median end-to-end latency increase of ~6ms for single-tool calls due to idempotency checks, but multi-tool parallel calls saw a 22% reduction in observed duplicate side-effects and a 12% improvement in 99th percentile streaming stability in our multiplexing demo. Checklist: - [x] API spec and SDK shims implemented - [x] Observability added - [x] Integration tests added - [x] Migration guide written - [x] Benchmarks and rollout plan documented QA and verification steps: run example-apps/multiplexing-demo against local stack, validate no duplicate side-effects for simulated retries, run tool-composition integration test under stress, verify CI e2e pass. Security review: idempotency tokens are scoped per-customer and rotated via KMS; we added a short section in docs on token lifecycle. Known limitations: long-running tools that stream their own state must adopt the provisional-result pattern; we added examples in the migration doc. Relationship to other work: builds on ENG-2191 (tool orchestration primitives) and complements ENG-2248 (streaming stability improvements).
review_comments: Evan Mills: Overall approach looks solid. Question: can the rebuffer window be dynamically tuned per-model? Please add a config hook.
Priya Natarajan (author): Added dynamic rebuffer config and documented defaults in docs; small follow-up in commit 5.
Rita Patel: Concern about storage of provisional results for large binary blobs — can we stream-to-temp-s3 and store pointer? Suggest adding garbage-collection TTL.
Priya Natarajan (author): Implemented pointer-based provisional storage and GC TTL; updated tests to simulate object pointers.
Jonas Berg: CI flaked initially on the e2e step due to clock skew in the idempotency token test. After forcing NTP in the runner it passed. Approved.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the external helper names used by OpenAI-compatible clients but changes semantics for injection timing; teams should plan a short migration window to validate workflows that relied on mid-stream observable side effects.
